title: Routing Record
description: One line of the graph execution log (JSONL, append-only, one record per event). The replayability contract: every routing decision is logged with enough context that a run can be reconstructed and a misroute diagnosed as a graph bug rather than a mystery. This log is also the raw input to the eval layer (latency, fan-out width, retry counts, escalation frequency all derive from it).

seq.description: Monotonic per-run sequence number assigned by the single log writer; total order of events even when wall clocks collide.

type.description: code nodes exist because deterministic work (parsing, dedup, filtering) never runs through the model. gate nodes include verify gates and the adversarial verifier. human nodes are approval/escalation points.

role.description: Optional functional role, orthogonal to type. type is the execution kind (a verifier is type=model: prompted, budgeted, retried on infra failure); role marks its function (gate: its success/failure opens/blocks the run). Added in 0.4.0 so consumers can distinguish model producers from model gates without parsing reason text.

event.description: enter/exit bracket node execution. spawn records each child at a fan-out; join records the sync gate resolving. retry/escalate/rollback/fail are the bounded-cycle events.

parent_node_id.description: Set on spawn: the fan-out node that created this child.

decision.description: Required for event=route: which edge and why.

alternatives.description: Edges that were available but not taken; what makes a misroute diagnosable.

scope.description: Declared on enter for model nodes. Write sets define fan-out independence: siblings spawned by the same fanout must have disjoint writes (conformance-checkable from this log). Read overlap is fine — shared reads are what the harness cache is for.

attempt.description: Required for event=retry. Semantics (defined in 0.4.0; previously ambiguous): number is the retry being issued, 1-based — the first retry after the initial attempt is number=1, and retry records run 1..max-1. Total attempts consumed at exhaustion equals max, and the escalation record/report counts that total. Every cycle carries a limit; a retry record without max is a conformance failure.

inputs_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical serialization of the node's input artifacts; makes replay comparisons cheap (same digest in, different route out = graph nondeterminism to investigate).

checkpoint.description: Present on enter (the state a rollback restores to) and on rollback (the state restored).

git_ref.description: Resolved commit SHA (7-40 hex). Symbolic refs (HEAD, branch names) are forbidden: a checkpoint must be an immutable restore point, and a moving pointer makes rollback and replay meaningless. (0.4.0: pattern added after a real implementation emitted 'HEAD' and the unconstrained string permitted it.)

verify_ref.description: Id of the verify-result that justified this event (e.g. the fail that triggered a retry, the pass that opened a gate).

merge.description: Structured merge outcome, for join events and for exit events that conclude a merge. Added in 0.4.0: merge destinations were previously smuggled through detail as free text.

target.description: Branch or ref merged into, e.g. 'graph/<run-id>/integration'.

result_ref.description: Resolved SHA of the merge result (the new tip).

failure_kind.description: Optional on fail/escalate/rollback events. Distinguishes, machine-readably, a gate doing its job (gate_finding: the adversarial verifier found a bug — desired behavior, run fails) from infrastructure failure (runner crash/timeout — retried, then escalated). Added in 0.4.0: this distinction previously lived only in free-form reason text.
